item.title: Chinese vice premier to attend 11th Eastern Economic Forum, hold meetings of China-Russia cooperation committees and 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum in Russia
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BEIJING, Aug. 31 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will travel to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum and hold the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum from September 2 to 4, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Monday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, was invited by the government of the Russian Federation, the spokesperson added.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BEIJING, Aug. 31 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council executive meeting in Beijing on Monday. The meeting studied and implemented the guiding principles of remarks made by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, at a recent Party leadership meeting on rescue and relief work following a devastating mudslide that struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26. Emphasizing the need to fully implement key emergency rescue and response tasks, the meeting called for continued all-out efforts to search for and rescue missing persons while guarding against secondary disasters. It also urged stronger monitoring and early warning, as well as active international coordination and cooperation. Efforts should be intensified to identify and address risks of all kinds and further strengthen emergency management capabilities to prevent major and particularly serious disasters, safeguard people's lives and property, and maintain social stability, according to the meeting. The meeting also reviewed progress in developing urban underground pipeline networks. Stressing that such networks are a key component of modern infrastructure, the meeting called for efforts to accelerate their development in a systematic approach, eliminate safety hazards at the source, and enhance the quality and functionality of urban areas. The meeting studied measures to promote the high-quality development of attracting investment. It emphasized the need to clearly define government practices that are encouraged or prohibited in this regard and to further regulate local governments' economic promotion activities. Pursuing investment should focus more on improving the business environment, fostering industrial ecosystems and providing high-quality administrative services, according to the meeting. The meeting discussed and approved in principle a draft amendment to the law on the administration of tax collection and decided to submit it to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for deliberation. It called for efforts to improve tax services, better protect taxpayers' lawful rights and interests, promote tax fairness, and enhance fiscal and taxation governance. The meeting also reviewed and approved a draft amendment to the regulations for implementing the audit law.

item.title: China ready to advance hand in hand along path of modernization with Mongolia, says Xi
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China is ready to work with Mongolia to foster more areas of growth for mutually beneficial cooperation and advance hand in hand along the respective paths of modernization. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Noting that China and Mongolia are close neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, Xi said that peaceful coexistence, mutual support and solidarity as well as mutually beneficial cooperation have always been the mainstream and defining feature of bilateral relations. China will continue to place China-Mongolia relations in an important position in its neighborhood diplomacy, and work together with Mongolia to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and promote people-to-people connectivity, so as to inject greater vitality into the comprehensive strategic partnership and promote the building of the China-Mongolia community with a shared future, Xi said. Both sides should consolidate the political foundation for the development of China-Mongolia relations, respect each other's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns, Xi said. Xi voiced China's readiness to strengthen alignment of development strategies with Mongolia, promote traditional cooperation in trade, connectivity as well as energy and mineral resources, and explore the potential for cooperation in emerging fields such as green minerals, artificial intelligence and the digital economy. China hopes that Mongolia will effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, said Xi, urging both sides to strengthen coordination and cooperation in multilateral affairs and jointly address global challenges. Khurelsukh, for his part, said that Mongolia and China are friendly neighbors who have always respected and trusted each other and maintained good-neighborly relations, regardless of changes in the international situation. China's development has provided major opportunities for neighboring countries and is driving the development of Asia and the world, he added. Deepening friendly cooperation with China is a top priority of Mongolia's foreign policy, he said, adding that Mongolia stands ready to continuously consolidate political mutual trust with China, enhance cooperation in trade and investment, industry, agriculture, mining and the green economy, and advance bilateral relations to new heights. Mongolia firmly adheres to the one-China principle and recognizes that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory, while issues related to Xinjiang, Xizang and Hong Kong are China's internal affairs, he said. The four major global initiatives proposed by Xi and the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity are of great significance for maintaining world peace and security, promoting sustainable development and addressing global challenges, he said, adding that Mongolia stands ready to work with China to jointly implement them.

item.title: Xi says China ready to work with Uzbekistan to usher in new 'golden decade' for bilateral relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Uzbekistan to usher in a new "golden decade" for bilateral relations, as the two sides celebrate the 10th anniversary of the China-Uzbekistan comprehensive strategic partnership. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Under the leadership of the two heads of state, bilateral relations have continued to improve and upgrade, with fruitful cooperation across various fields and notable progress in building a China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Uzbekistan to consolidate strategic mutual trust and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, Xi added. Xi stressed that no matter how the international situation changes, China's commitment to deepening bilateral friendship will remain unwavering, and China will continue to support Uzbekistan in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions. Xi called on the two sides to work together to advance bilateral cooperation. He said the two sides should pursue high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, expand cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence and anti-desertification, and uphold mutual benefit and win-win outcomes. Efforts should also be made to sustain the momentum of local-level exchanges, accelerate the establishment of cultural centers in each other's countries, expand cooperation in fields including education and poverty reduction, and promote mutual understanding between the two peoples, Xi said. The two sides should make good use of their law enforcement and security cooperation mechanisms, work together to combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, and strengthen the security barrier, Xi said. As founding members of the SCO, China and Uzbekistan should work together to fully implement the outcomes of the Tianjin Summit and promote development and prosperity in the region, Xi said. Mirziyoyev, for his part, extended warm congratulations on China's continuous major development achievements under Xi's leadership, noting that China has responded to global challenges with confidence and resolve. He expressed full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization. Uzbekistan and China share a profound friendship and have always understood and supported each other, he said, noting that Xi's vision has opened up broad prospects for Uzbekistan-China relations and guided the comprehensive development of cooperation in various fields between the two sides. Mirziyoyev added that Uzbekistan remains unwavering in its commitment to developing relations with China, a position that will not change regardless of how the international situation evolves. Uzbekistan stands ready to work with China to deepen political mutual trust, expand trade and investment, enhance cooperation in fields such as agriculture, transportation, energy, minerals, science and technology, promote people-to-people exchanges, jointly combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, and bring bilateral relations to a higher level, said Mirziyoyev. Uzbekistan firmly adheres to the one-China principle, highly recognizes the four global initiatives proposed by Xi, and is ready to join hands with China to promote the development of the SCO and jointly safeguard international fairness and justice, Mirziyoyev said.

item.title: Xi expects stronger foundation, brighter future for China-Russia ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that, under his and Russian President Vladimir Putin's strategic guidance and through the joint efforts of both sides, the foundation of China-Russia relations will become ever stronger, their progress ever steadier, and their future ever brighter. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Xi said that during the successful state visit of Putin to China in May, he and Putin made arrangements to steer bilateral relations toward higher-quality and higher-level development from a strategic and long-term perspective, and reached consensus on deepening cooperation between China and Russia across various sectors under the new circumstances. The competent authorities of the two countries are actively implementing the consensus, with substantial results already made, Xi said, adding that exchanges and cooperation between the two sides have maintained a strong momentum. Xi noted that the international landscape is witnessing a notable increase in uncertain and unpredictable factors, against the backdrop of accelerating profound changes unseen in a century. But the pursuit of people across the world of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes remains unchanged, he added. The SCO shoulders the important responsibility for safeguarding regional stability and promoting regional development, he said. China, he said, stands ready to work with Russia and other parties to jointly chart the course for the development of the SCO, help ensure its steady and sustained progress, and strengthen the driving force for reform of global governance and the advancement of an equal and orderly multipolar world. Amid a turbulent and complex international landscape, Russia and China have continuously deepened their comprehensive strategic coordination, upholding equality, mutual trust, and mutual support, while cooperation and development across various fields have advanced rapidly, and Russia-China relations have become a model for relations between countries, Putin said. Russia is willing to maintain high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade, energy, industry, transportation, and science and technology, enhance people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and promote bilateral relations to achieve new results, he said. Through the joint efforts of all parties, the SCO has evolved into a dynamic and efficient regional cooperation platform with significant international influence, said Putin, noting that Russia and China should continuously strengthen their solidarity and cooperation within the organization and play a guiding role. Russia is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with China within multilateral mechanisms such as the United Nations, the BRICS mechanism and the G20, support China in hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, and jointly uphold world peace, stability and prosperity, he said. The two heads of state also exchanged views on international and regional issues of common concern.

item.title: Xi, Japarov chart new course for China-Kyrgyzstan ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said here on Monday that China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to deliver more practical cooperation outcomes that are tangible and accessible. Xi made the remarks during talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi landed in Bishkek on Sunday for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026. The visit came as the China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation has ushered in a "golden period" of rapid development, as noted by Xi in a written speech delivered upon his arrival, with the two countries working to translate their longstanding friendship and strong political mutual trust into broader cooperation and greater benefits for their people. DEEPENING TRUST, BUILDING A SHARED FUTURE The visit coincides with the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence. On behalf of the Chinese government and people, Xi first extended greetings to Japarov on the occasion of Kyrgyzstan's Independence Day. Xi said that in recent years, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have achieved leapfrog development under the joint guidance of the two leaders, with cooperation across all fields flourishing, boosting the development of both countries and bringing benefits to their people, while also contributing to peace, stability and prosperity in the region. Xi noted that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). China is building a great country in all respects and advancing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, Xi said, noting that Kyrgyzstan is also making every effort to implement its National Development Program until 2030. China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to strengthen the alignment of development strategies, deepen exchanges on governance experience, and make substantive progress in building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, he added. Xi noted that high-level political mutual trust and firm mutual support are crucial to ensuring the steady and sustained development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. China firmly supports Kyrgyzstan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, as well as pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said, adding that China stands ready to work with the Kyrgyz side to continue firmly supporting each other on issues involving each other's core interests. For his part, Japarov said he was honored to welcome Xi to Kyrgyzstan on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The visit further demonstrated the profound friendship and high-level political mutual trust between Kyrgyzstan and China, and marked an important milestone in the history of bilateral relations, he said. Japarov said Kyrgyzstan and China are neighboring countries, and the ancient Silk Road has closely connected the two nations. In recent years, with the rapid development of the Kyrgyzstan-China comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, bilateral relations have entered a golden period and reached an unprecedented level, he said. He expressed gratitude to China for its selfless support and assistance at every critical moment in Kyrgyzstan's development, while extending warm congratulations on the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC and the launch of the implementation of China's 15th Five-Year Plan. Japarov also expressed admiration for the remarkable development achievements China has made under the leadership of Xi, and voiced willingness to learn from China's experience in state governance, particularly Xi's commitment to the people, as embodied in his words, "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." China has always been a priority in Kyrgyzstan's foreign policy, as well as Kyrgyzstan's closest friend and most reliable partner, Japarov said, noting that Kyrgyzstan firmly adheres to the one-China principle and stands ready to further develop good-neighborly and friendly relations with China on the basis of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit. EXPANDING PRACTICAL COOPERATION, DELIVERING TANGIBLE BENEFITS Xi urged the two countries to deepen practical cooperation, effectively implement the intergovernmental economic and trade cooperation plan, diversify trade products and develop new growth areas such as digital trade and cross-border e-commerce. Xi also said the two sides should ensure the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, calling it a major transportation artery that carries the development aspirations of the people across the region. He called for modernizing border ports and deepening "soft connectivity" in institutions, standards and rules, and urged the launch of more landmark projects in renewable energy, resource recycling and other fields, the implementation of cooperation documents on green minerals, and cooperation across the entire industrial chain. Xi said China and Kyrgyzstan should make joint efforts to successfully build the Belt and Road Joint Laboratory, enhance artificial intelligence cooperation, and leverage scientific and technological innovation to boost the quality and efficiency of bilateral cooperation. The two sides should further facilitate exchanges and expand cooperation in youth affairs, media, tourism, sports, health care and local affairs, while continuing to strengthen the social and public support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship, Xi added. For his part, Japarov said Kyrgyzstan is willing to strengthen cooperation with China in trade and investment, connectivity, technological innovation, energy, mineral resources and the green economy, as well as deepen exchanges in education, health, culture and youth sectors. Kyrgyzstan is ready to actively advance the construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, so as to turn it into a "steel Silk Road" for the new era and a new bond of friendship between the two countries, Japarov said. JOINING HANDS FOR PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT China and Kyrgyzstan should expand cooperation in law enforcement and security, work together to combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, extremism and separatism, drug trafficking and transnational crimes, and jointly maintain regional peace and stability, Xi said. China supports Kyrgyzstan in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs, Xi said, noting that China is willing to further enhance collaboration with Kyrgyzstan within the framework of the United Nations, jointly implement the four major global initiatives, oppose hegemonism and power politics, adhere to true multilateralism, safeguard international fairness and justice, and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Noting that China and Kyrgyzstan are both founding members of the SCO, Xi said the two countries should promote the implementation of the outcomes of the Tianjin Summit, facilitate common development in the region, and advance the development of the SCO to a new level. For his part, Japarov said that the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi help countries work together to address common challenges and build a more just and stable international order. Kyrgyzstan stands ready to closely coordinate with China on multilateral platforms, including the United Nations, the SCO, the China-Central Asia mechanism and the World AI Cooperation Organization, to jointly safeguard world peace and stability, Japarov said. Following the talks, the two heads of state signed a joint declaration of the People's Republic of China and the Kyrgyz Republic on the high-quality development of the comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era and a bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation. The signing of the bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will provide an important legal foundation for the everlasting friendship and firm mutual support between the two countries, Xi said. Echoing Xi, Japarov said the signing of the treaty will open up broader prospects for bilateral relations. They also jointly witnessed the exchange of bilateral cooperation documents in the fields of investment, transportation, customs, and sister-city relations. During the visit, the two sides also signed over 20 cooperation documents covering science and technology, education, culture, media, and other areas.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.

item.title: China sees growth in new foreign-invested firms, high-tech FDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 -- China recorded an increase in newly established foreign-invested enterprises and robust growth in foreign direct investment (FDI) in high-tech industries in the first seven months of 2026, despite a decline in overall inflows, official data showed Friday. During the period, 37,711 new foreign-invested enterprises were set up, up 4.4 percent year on year, while FDI in actual use came in at 438.33 billion yuan (about 64.63 billion U.S. dollars), down 6.2 percent from a year earlier, the Ministry of Commerce said. By sector, manufacturing attracted 109.43 billion yuan in FDI, while the service sector drew 319.95 billion yuan. Despite the overall drop, FDI in high-tech industries surged 32.7 percent to 182.31 billion yuan, accounting for 41.6 percent of the national total, a rise of 12.2 percentage points from a year ago. Specifically, FDI in R&D and design services, services for the commercialization of sci-tech achievements, and electronic and telecommunications equipment manufacturing jumped 72.1 percent, 62.2 percent and 39.9 percent, respectively. During the same period, actual investment from Saudi Arabia, France and the Republic of Korea grew by 343.7 percent, 36.1 percent and 15.8 percent, respectively, with investment via free ports included in the calculations. In June, China unveiled a 15-measure action plan to stabilize and optimize foreign investment utilization, focusing on expanding market access, streamlining investment procedures, boosting investment promotion, strengthening services and safeguards for foreign investors, and improving foreign capital management. A new version of the Catalogue of Encouraged Industries for Foreign Investment, which took effect on Feb. 1 this year, aims to steer more foreign capital into advanced manufacturing, modern services, high-tech industries, energy conservation and environmental protection, as well as into the central, western and northeastern regions of the country.

item.title: China to revise regulations on housing provident fund management
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-18
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree publicizing a decision to revise the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund, which will take effect on Sept. 20, 2026. According to the decision, the scope of the fund's withdrawal and use will be expanded. For those withdrawing from the housing provident fund to pay rent, the eligibility threshold requiring rent to exceed a prescribed proportion of a household's wage income will be removed. Housing provident fund savings can be withdrawn for new purposes under the revised regulations, including renovating the homes the contributors live in and paying property management fees for such homes. The decision also states that the channels for the investment and utilization of the housing provident fund will be appropriately broadened, specifying that housing provident fund management centers are allowed to use the funds to purchase policy-oriented financial bonds. To enhance the efficiency of management services, the decision also underscores efforts to simplify the procedures for employees to apply for housing provident fund withdrawals and to shorten the review period for housing provident fund loan applications. The decision, which strengthens risk prevention and control, stipulates that housing provident fund management centers should establish comprehensive, complete and accurate credit records and incorporate them into the national credit information sharing platform. Amid efforts to expand the coverage of the system, the decision clarifies that individual business owners, part-time employees and other people in flexible employment can pay voluntary contributions into the housing provident fund and enjoy policy support in accordance with the regulations.
